mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License of the WFOE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) under the State Administration for Market Regulation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path if destination is an Apostille Convention state: notarize the Business License before a Chinese notary public and authenticate through a single Hague Apostille issued by the competent provincial Foreign Affairs Office. Taiwan non-member path: notarize the Business License, obtain verification from the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), and complete consular legalization at the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO). The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never combine or chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (NECIPS compliance extract equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local Administration for Market Regulation / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path if destination is an Apostille Convention state: print and notarize the official compliance extract, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the provincial Foreign Affairs Office. Taiwan non-member path: notarize the extract, obtain SEF verification, and complete TECRO consular legalization. Only the single path required by the receiving jurisdiction may be used; apostille and consular legalization are never sequential or cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation agents and franchise document signing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path if destination is an Apostille Convention state: notarize the signed Board Resolution and Power of Attorney before a Chinese notary public, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the provincial Foreign Affairs Office. Taiwan non-member path: notarize the documents, obtain SEF verification, and complete TECRO consular legalization. The routes are alternative, not cumulative; do not chain apostille and legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: WFOE incorporators and board at formation, filed with the Administration for Market Regulation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path if destination is an Apostille Convention state: notarize the filed Articles of Association and obtain a Hague Apostille from the provincial Foreign Affairs Office. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming corporate account relationship and payment conduct

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, franchise master licensees and material royalty payors must be screened at inception and on a continuous basis against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions and terrorist designation list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Taiwan financial regulator AML/CFT notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons and their family members, close associates, and shell-company intermediaries for 24 months after leaving public office. Fuzzy-match hits above 95% probability and adverse media flags must be escalated to the AML compliance officer, documented, and resolved before incorporation; transaction monitoring must remain in place for the life of the WFOE.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended, particularly Articles 1, 6, 15, 17, 18, 20, 128, 156, 172, 192, 202, 228 and 419; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; Regulations Governing Permission of Investment by Mainland Areas Persons (applicable to mainland Chinese shareholders); Fair Trade Act and Food Safety and Sanitation Act for operational licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, with joint approval by the Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign and mainland capital in Taiwan.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation, filed through the MOEA Company and Business Registration One-Stop Online System, resulting in the Certificate of Incorporation and government-issued unified company identification number.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Taiwan Company Act no statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed. However, the MOEA Investment Commission may require the stated capital to be reasonably commensurate with the proposed business plan, and the foreign or mainland investor must remit the capital from abroad in foreign currency, convert it into New Taiwan Dollars, deposit it in a domestic bank account established for the company, and complete capital verification before company registration is finalized. No blocked escrow account is required after capital verification, but foreign exchange remittance entries must be reported and capital may not be repatriated except as legally distributable profits or approved investment exits.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the proposed form of the Articles of Incorporation and all related incorporation documents are hereby approved, ratified, and adopted as the constitutive documents of the Company, and the sole shareholder is directed to execute and file the same with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the authorized share capital of the Company is fixed at NT$1,000,000, divided into 100,000 ordinary registered shares of NT$10 each, of which 100,000 shares are subscribed for cash by the sole shareholder, representing 100% of the Company's equity, and such subscription is accepted in full. The full subscription price shall be paid into a newly opened corporate bank account and shall remain unwithdrawable until the capital verification report is issued and the company registration is completed, after which the funds may be used as working capital in accordance with the approved business plan. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [registered address], Taiwan, and the Company is authorized to execute a lease, accept service of legal process, and file the office address with all competent authorities. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the corporate seal and company chop of the Company shall be produced and held in the joint custody of the Chairman and the General Manager; all instruments, contracts, cheques and bank mandates executed by the Company must bear the corporate seal and the signature of two authorized directors. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as Chairman and authorized legal representative, [Name] is appointed as General Manager, and [Name] is appointed as Company Secretary, each for a term of three years and subject to removal by shareholders; the directors approve compensation within statutory limits. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as the independent certified public accountant of the Company for the current fiscal year, and the accountant is instructed to conduct an annual audit and provide a statutory audit report. RESOLVED FURTHER, that a bank account shall be opened at [Bank], and the Chairman, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer are designated as authorized signatories, with any two signatures required for disbursements exceeding NT$500,000. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Manager is authorized and directed to complete tax registration, labor insurance registration, food business registration, franchise disclosure compliance, environmental registration if triggered, fire safety certification, and all other statutory filings needed before commencement of business operations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all acts performed by the incorporator on behalf of the Company prior to this meeting are hereby ratified, confirmed and adopted as acts of the Company. RESOLVED, that the first board meeting is adjourned sine die.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business, Franchise, Fire Safety, and Environmental Clearances Before Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare; local municipal or county Health Bureau; local Fire Department under the Ministry of Interior; local Environmental Protection Bureau under the Environmental Protection Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing revenue operations, obtain the Food Business Registration Certificate from the local health bureau by submitting the completed food sanitation application, food facility layout plan, equipment sanitation list, food handler health certificates, and proof of premises. If the company manufactures syrup concentrate in a commercial production facility, apply for a Food Factory Registration with the TFDA under the Food Safety and Sanitation Act. Prepare a franchise disclosure statement compliant with the Fair Trade Act for all prospective franchisees. Apply for fire safety certification and schedule the mandatory inspection by the local Fire Department, covering the cooking area, emergency lighting, exits, and automatic fire suppression systems. Verify whether an Environmental Registration Declaration is required by the local Environmental Protection Bureau based on wastewater and VOC thresholds; if required, submit the declaration and monitoring plan before tests are run.
required_dossiers: Food facility floor plan and sanitation checklist
Franchise disclosure statement, if franchise offers are made
Fire safety equipment and inspection certificate
Structural approval for counters, syrup tanks, and racks
Wastewater discharge permit application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the health or fire inspection fails, complete the corrective actions, hire a certified technician for re-verification, and request re-inspection within ten working days. If the environmental registration is rejected because emissions thresholds are exceeded, commence a full Fixed Pollution Source Permit application or Environmental Impact Assessment as required by the Environmental Protection Administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA); local municipal and county Health Bureaus; local Fire Department under the Ministry of Interior; local Environmental Protection Bureau under the Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration Certificate under Article 8 of the Food Safety and Sanitation Act, Food Factory Registration for syrup concentrate manufacturing, and Franchise Disclosure and Agreement Compliance under the Fair Trade Act for all domestic franchise offers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan, and the local municipal or county Environmental Protection Bureau with jurisdiction over water discharges and air emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration, Low Impact Category, with Full EIA Report Exempt, unless the syrup production line is characterized as a factory under the Factories Management Act with chemical use, wastewater discharge of at least 5 cubic metres per day, or volatile organic compound stack emissions of at least 0.6 kg per hour, in which case a Fixed Pollution Source Permit and full Environmental Impact Assessment may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to a municipal sanitary sewer must meet pH 6.0-9.0, biochemical oxygen demand BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand COD not exceeding 100 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 10 mg/L, and ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 10 mg/L. VOCs emitted from syrup heating, blending, and tea-making equipment must remain below 0.6 kg/hour stack limit. Hazardous waste generated above 20 kg per month must be stored in approved containers and removed by a licensed waste contractor under manifest control. Food waste and used cooking oil must be separated, labelled, and delivered to EPA-permitted disposal facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Equipment Certificate and Fire Safety Management Plan approval from the local Fire Department, confirmed by an on-site fire protection inspection before opening; installation of approved fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, exits, and automatic fire suppression systems in cooking and warehousing areas; building occupancy permit and structural load certification for tea counters, syrup storage racks, and commercial equipment; and workplace safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act covering electrical safety, machine guarding, ventilation, and employee health examinations for food handlers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, administered through the National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau) online taxpayer portal and the Golden Tax Project Phase IV electronic invoice system; local enforcement is performed by the municipal and provincial tax service branches where the WFOE is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Upon incorporation, the WFOE obtains a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the USCC is the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for all People's Republic of China taxes. Step 2: Within 30 days of issuance of the business license, the WFOE must complete post-incorporation tax registration at the competent local STA branch via the e-Tax Bureau, file taxpayer registration information, and activate the electronic taxpayer account. Step 3: For VAT, the WFOE is automatically registered as a taxpayer; it must operate as a Small-Scale VAT taxpayer or a General VAT taxpayer according to annual taxable turnover, with General VAT taxpayer registration becoming mandatory once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. Step 4: For a foreign non-resident enterprise, including a Taiwan shareholder or franchise counterparty, that is not incorporated in China but derives China-source income, the non-resident enterprise or its withholding agent must complete a Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Registration with the competent STA branch to obtain a non-resident tax identification number, thereby enabling withholding tax compliance and the application of treaty benefits. A foreign enterprise that merely purchases exported goods or services from the WFOE does not require a Chinese VAT registration; export VAT zero-rating is substantiated by the exporter's documentation rather than by a foreign VAT identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (China does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime; a WFOE is mandatorily taxed as a Chinese resident enterprise at the entity level). The only relevant elections are: (i) the election to remain a Small-Scale VAT taxpayer while annual taxable sales do not exceed RMB 5,000,000; (ii) the election to become a General VAT taxpayer after satisfying the prescribed conditions; and (iii) the application of the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Tax Evasion when the Taiwanese counterparty obtains a Taiwan tax residency certificate, to reduce or eliminate withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, and capital gains. No hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered by the State Taxation Administration under the Provisional Regulations of the People's Republic of China on VAT and the VAT reform pilot measures replacing Business Tax with VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All business entities must complete tax registration upon incorporation irrespective of turnover. The mandatory General VAT taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000; below this threshold the taxpayer may remain a Small-Scale VAT taxpayer. For franchise and licensing services the standard VAT rate is 6%, while the headline rate for edible syrups and beverage goods is 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory real-time invoice data clearance regime under the Golden Tax Project Phase IV. General VAT taxpayers must issue Special VAT Invoices or Ordinary VAT Invoices through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Invoice Service Platform; fully digitalised electronic invoices carry an STA-assigned tax-control digital signature and anti-counterfeiting QR code, and invoice data are cleared to the STA tax-control system on a near-real-time basis through taxpayer application programming interfaces. The e-Tax Bureau portal requires mandatory filing of VAT returns, special invoice certification, and export tax rebate declarations. Export sales to a separate customs territory such as Taiwan are substantiated by the electronic transmission of Customs export declaration data to the tax authority; no VAT is collected on the export invoice and the exporter reclaims input VAT through the electronic export rebate workflow.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods, including beverage syrups, boba ingredients, and franchise-related equipment sold by the WFOE to franchisees in Taiwan or other destinations, are zero-rated for Chinese VAT provided that: (i) the goods are physically exported from the customs territory of China and declared to Customs; (ii) the exporter is a registered VAT general taxpayer; (iii) the goods are supported by a genuine sales contract and commercial invoice; (iv) title and risk have passed to the overseas buyer; (v) the export proceeds are collected and repatriated into a domestic bank account within the statutory 180-day period; and (vi) the export VAT refund declaration is filed with matching Customs and foreign-exchange evidence. Qualifying cross-border services, such as certain intangible property licensing, franchise know-how, and information-technology services, may be zero-rated or exempt when the services are supplied wholly outside China to non-resident enterprises and are listed in the STA's cross-border taxable services zero-rating and exemption catalogue; as with goods, outward payment evidence and overseas consumption documentation must be retained. Pure trademark-franchise royalty receivables that do not qualify for zero-rating remain subject to 6% VAT, and the substantive qualification must be confirmed with the competent STA branch.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Export / Export Goods Customs Declaration Form) data matched by Customs to the VAT exporter
Commercial Export Invoice and the electronic export invoice generated in the e-Tax Bureau export invoice module
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the goods leaving the customs territory of China
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt confirmation evidencing repatriation of export proceeds to the WFOE's domestic bank account
Export sales contract or franchise purchase order containing trade terms
Export VAT refund declaration electronically filed with the STA and the matching export tax rebate list
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Article 66 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Levy and Recovery, obtaining an export tax refund by means of false export declarations, forged documentation, or other deceptive conduct is punished by recovery of the refunded tax, a fine of not less than 100% and not more than 500% of the refunded tax, and where the conduct constitutes a crime, referral for criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which may lead to serious custodial sentences. Separately, if export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period and no officially recognised deferral or deemed-collection exception applies, the STA will claw back any VAT zero-rating benefit previously granted, assess a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on the recovered tax from the refund date, and impose additional administrative penalties. The exporter's tax credit rating may be downgraded to Class D, triggering intensified audit scrutiny, cash-based tax controls, and temporary suspension of export tax rebate eligibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), operating through its delegated State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), is the competent central bank and foreign exchange regulatory authority for all onshore banking and cross-border capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi (CNY) is not freely convertible under the capital account, despite being convertible for most current account transactions such as trade receipts, royalties, and service payments once the underlying authenticity is verified by a designated bank. The WFOE must establish a SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account to receive inbound equity capital from the Taiwan shareholder; these funds are classified as capital account income and cannot be converted into CNY without a compliant capital account settlement process that complies with the positive list and negative list regime. Registered capital proceeds may not be used for entrusted loans, securities investment, real estate beyond the approved business scope, or non-operating speculative activities. Profit remittances from the WFOE to the Taiwan parent are permitted under the current account if the remittance is supported by audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, board resolutions, and the required foreign exchange declaration; however, the bank must verify that the profits are truly earned, the corporate income tax and dividends withholding tax obligations have been fulfilled, and no unreported offshore liabilities are present. Export proceeds must be repatriated into China and either retained in a foreign exchange account or settled into RMB voluntarily; mandatory forced surrender is not applied. Overall, the regime is one of managed convertibility with tight documentary verification, purpose-code monitoring, and strict sequestration of capital account funds until compliant conversion is achieved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds generated by the WFOE from global franchise syrup and ingredient sales must be repatriated into mainland China within 180 days from the date of export declaration, unless a SAFE-approved extension is obtained. There is no mandatory conversion ratio requiring foreign currency export receipts to be sold to the central bank; instead, the WFOE may retain these receipts in a foreign currency current account with a designated domestic bank or voluntarily settle them into CNY at market-based rates. All repatriated export proceeds must be matched against China Customs declaration records and the underlying commercial contracts to verify authenticity before the bank processes the credit or settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI platforms such as Airwallex, Currenxie, or Payoneer have low viability as core treasury banking rails for a mainland China WFOE. These entities are generally not licensed depository institutions in China, cannot hold statutory RMB basic settlement accounts, cannot open SAFE-regulated foreign exchange capital accounts, and cannot file capital account conversion declarations. They also lack the necessary CNAPS clearing eligibility to settle local payroll, tax, social security, and domestic supplier payments in a compliant manner. Such EMIs may be used only as ancillary collection channels for overseas franchise royalty deposits from non-China territories, but even then the funds must eventually be routed into a domestic bank account with proper trade or service purpose codes. For the WFOE capital structure, the primary liquidity bandwidth must remain with a Tier-1 onshore commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For opening a RMB basic settlement account, the WFOE legal representative must appear physically in the domestic bank branch or send an authorized officer with a notarized and verified power of attorney; the bank will conduct a face-to-face beneficial ownership interview and verify the entity seal system. For the foreign currency capital account, physical presence of the legal representative or a senior authorized signatory at the Chinese branch is generally mandatory, and remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by mainstream Tier-1 banks for capital account purpose. Taiwan-origin corporate shareholders must complete cross-strait document authentication for company registry extracts, board resolutions, and identity evidence before the bank can complete enhanced due diligence. Video verification may supplement but cannot replace the in-branch identity and interview requirement for the statutory account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or opaque ownership chain in the Taiwan corporate shareholder, where the ultimate beneficial owner is hidden behind trust layers, familial cross-shareholdings, or a Hong Kong/Taiwan holding company structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and authenticated certificate of incorporation and articles of association for the Taiwan parent; full register of directors and shareholders; continuous beneficial ownership declaration identifying all natural persons holding more than 10%; copy of Taiwan ID or passport of each ultimate beneficial owner; certified copy of the share register for the past two years; bank reference letter from the Taiwan parent relationship bank; and a group structure chart explaining all intermediate ownership layers and reasons for the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound TWD or CNY capital injection for registered capital with insufficient source-of-funds evidence, raising possible third-party funding, disguised loans, unregistered offshore capital, or artificial round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth dossier comprising the Taiwan shareholder's audited financial statements for the last two years, 12 months of bank statements, tax clearance certificate, evidence of lawful accumulation of funds, board resolution approving the capital injection, capital contribution schedule aligned with the WFOE verification plan, signed undertaking that no nominee or back-to-back financing is used, and certified CPA capital verification report upon receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering concerns in the boba tea syrup, packaging, and franchise supply chain, particularly over/under-invoicing of related-party ingredient imports, false royalty calculations, or duplicate financing on the same shipment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction file per shipment including original commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, China Customs import declarations, customs duty and VAT payment receipts, third-party quality inspection certificates, franchise and trademark license agreements between the WFOE and Taiwan franchisor, transfer pricing documentation demonstrating arm's length pricing, warehouse in/out records, inventory reconciliation, and insurance certificates covering the relevant goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions list hits, PEP exposure, or unknown counterparty risk on the Taiwan patent/franchise royalty recipient or on any intermediary collection account linked to the global franchise system.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence report containing full sanctions and PEP screening against UN, OFAC, EU, UK, and China MOFCOM restricted lists; negative news search results; notarised identification for all beneficial owners of the royalty recipient; certified signature cards and mandate letters for all beneficiary collection accounts; a global royalty payment flow map showing jurisdictions, purpose codes, and tax withholdings; and an independent legal opinion confirming FATF compliance and the absence of shell-company red flags.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first complete SAFE foreign exchange registration in China and open a dedicated Foreign Currency Capital Account at a Tier-1 domestic bank. The Taiwan shareholder then routes the injection through SWIFT MT103 using the permitted purpose code for foreign-invested enterprise registered capital, with clear payment details referencing the WFOE name and SAFE registration number. Funds may arrive in USD, HKD, or CNY if the Taiwan side maintains a cross-border RMB clearing facility; TWD is generally not accepted as a direct onshore settlement currency, and USD or HKD is the recommended wiring currency. Upon receipt, the bank will provisionally credit the escrow capital account, the WFOE must commission a Chinese certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report, and only then may the funds be converted into RMB under SAFE positive-list rules. Capital account settlement proceeds must be transferred to the WFOE operating account and allocated solely for approved purposes such as warehousing, equipment, franchise system build-out, raw material procurement, and working capital; prohibited uses include security investments, entrusted loans, and real estate speculation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payments to Taiwan suppliers and the global franchise network, the WFOE should primarily use SWIFT MT103 for royalty remittances, raw material imports, and routine operational trade settlement. For large or letter-of-credit-driven imports of syrup, packaging, and machinery, the WFOE may issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit through its Chinese bank in favour of the Taiwan exporter, or use documentary collections for lower-risk open-account transactions. All cross-border payments must carry the correct SAFE/CFMMC purpose code, supported by commercial invoices, contracts, import customs declarations for goods, and tax-withholding certificates for royalty payments. Royalty remittances to the Taiwan franchisor require the WFOE to withhold Corporate Income Tax on royalties and pay VAT/business tax obligations before the bank releases the remittance. Locally, franchise outlets settle RMB receipts through CNAPS-enabled POS terminals and e-wallets, with daily clearing into the WFOE's RMB operating account for inventory replenishment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward sale and purchase contracts with a designated Chinese bank, used for hedging genuine current account and approved capital account exposures such as USD-denominated import invoices and foreign-currency royalties
Cross-currency swaps between CNY and USD or HKD for hedging underlying investment or operating cash flows, subject to SAFE real-demand background documentation and bank limit approval
CNY FX options for commercial transaction hedging, including call and put options that are settleable on a deliverable basis with the underlying trade exposure

NDFs are not permissible as onshore instruments for the mainland WFOE because CNY is deliverable for current account transactions; offshore RMB NDF structures may exist in the Taiwan or Hong Kong market but cannot be booked or settled by the mainland entity without breaching SAFE constraints

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax (PSEIT) on taxable income; retained-earnings surtax of 5% on undistributed surplus (additional tax, not an incentive). Alternative Minimum Tax at 12% applies under the Income Basic Tax Act with a basic income exemption of NT$500,000. Statutory incentives: R&D expenditure tax credit of up to 15% of eligible R&D spending under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, capped at 30% of tax payable; emerging-industry investment credits; accelerated depreciation for energy-saving and automated equipment; 10-year loss carryforward for entities maintaining complete accounting records and filing audited returns on time.
